tagline: Down the ridge between two lakes, on the old bison road.
intro: The Trace leaves Grand Rivers, on the neck of land between Kentucky Lake and Lake Barkley, and runs 43 miles south down the ridge between them to Dover, Tennessee. Before the dams there were no lakes, only two rivers and the country between, known since the 1830s or so as Between the Rivers.

Making a recreation area of it meant moving everyone out. Golden Pond, Tharpe and Model were abandoned. The Tennessee end of the road was renamed The Trace, short for Buffalo Trace, after the old bison paths, and from the 1970s on, bison were brought back.

moments.title: Grand Rivers
moments.text: The town once stood at the narrowest point between the Cumberland and the Tennessee. The rivers are lakes now, and Grand Rivers sits on the isthmus.

moments.title: Golden Pond
moments.text: Known nationally for its moonshine in Prohibition, emptied of its last residents in 1969, and now the address of a planetarium and a 700-acre prairie where elk and bison roam.

moments.title: The Homeplace
moments.text: A living-history farm of the 1850s with 14 original buildings, and bison on the South Bison Range across the Trace.

practical: The Elk & Bison Prairie's 3.5-mile paved loop is open sunrise to sunset to enclosed vehicles only, with no motorcycles, bicycles or walkers.
